metadata.title: Morning After
metadata.description: Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit.

scene_001.title: January
scene_001.narration: The dorm heat hisses. You blink awake, the winter light harsh. The silence feels heavy after the break. Your heart tightens remembering Kensington. Your cousin's warnings, mother's guilt, the old friend's voice offering pills 'just for the holiday stress.' Classes start tomorrow, the pressure to 'do better this semester' thumps in your skull, words from your father.

resource_link.description: Irritability and fatigue are normal in early-year recovery.

choices.label: Scroll through Tumblr for an hour

resource_link.description: Avoidance can worsen cravings over time.

scene_002a.title: Late January
scene_002a.narration: You rush between lectures, your chest tightening. You scribble notes, but your focus drifts. After class, your Bio lab partner, Chloe, asks, 'You okay? You look wiped.' You hate how easily people notice. You can feel your hairline start to collect moisture, and you instinctively begin cracking your knuckles.

scene_002b.title: Avoidance Spiral
scene_002b.narration: You miss breakfast and rush to class late. Your professor frowns but says nothing. This is the fourth time already. Later, you overhear two classmates whispering about how 'you always look spaced.' Shame punches you in the gut.

resource_link.description: Negative self-conscious emotions, including shame and guilt, result from appraisal of how an experience pertains to the self in relation to others.

scene_003a.title: A Quiet Evening
scene_003a.narration: You're studying when a drilling wave of hunger climbs your spine. You grip the desk until it passes. You whisper: 'I'm okay. I'm okay.' When was the last time you ate?

choices.label: Skip dinner, your stomach is in knots

resource_link.description: Up to 50% of individuals with eating disorders use alcohol or illicit drugs.

scene_003b.title: Shame Always Gets In
scene_003b.narration: You lie awake. Lying to Chloe gnaws at you. You remember your therapist saying shame distorts your sense of worth, common among people with early childhood trauma. You wrap your fingers around your wrist.

scene_003c.title: Ducking Responsibilities
scene_003c.narration: You wander outside, cold air burning your nose. An email from your advisor telling you that your grades were starting to reflect your 'lack of performance' was looming in your head. It cut through you, almost as if all of your attempts to be perfect thus far will amount to nothing. You need to feel something.

choices.label: Open old messages from your dealer

scene_004a.title: Small Victories
scene_004a.narration: You turn in an assignment on time. Professor Sullivan nods approvingly. 'Good work.' It's small, but it feels like sunlight.

choices.label: Celebrate with tea at the café
Push yourself to keep working for that approval

resource_link.description: Balance is hard for any person to find, but it can be especially difficult for those who take on more than they are realistically capable of and hold themselves to an impossible-to-reach standard.

scene_004b.title: The Message
scene_004b.narration: Your old friend replies instantly: 'I'm around. If you ever need anything, I got you.' Your chest tightens. You know exactly what 'anything' means.

resource_link.description: Good friends are not only important as a way for a former drug user to voice frustrations about life in recovery, but they are also integral during that person's journey in recreating a new life for themselves.

scene_004c.title: Growing Distance
scene_004c.narration: You try to study, but Chloe doesn't sit next to you anymore. Nobody does. Many only know you from the time you completely blacked out at the sophomore homecoming frat party. You feel the separation widening.

choices.label: Let the friendship fade. It's her fault anyway

resource_link.description: Too much time on one's own can foment powerful senses of boredom, anxiety, and loneliness, as well as precipitate the return of painful memories, against which substances provide a means of relief.

scene_005a.title: You're Trying
scene_005a.narration: You attend an on-campus recovery meeting. The room smells like coffee and peppermint gum. Someone talks about the difficulty of staying sober despite wanting to be. You nod silently.

resource_link.description: There are safe and effective ways to recover from SUDs. Finding the right treatment option can be the key to a successful recovery journey.

scene_005b.title: Overworking
scene_005b.narration: You push through readings until your eyes blur. Exhaustion can be as dangerous as temptation.

resource_link.description: Several epidemiological studies indicate that regular caffeine intake creates dependence, which in part depends on withdrawal symptoms.

scene_005c.title: The Craving Surface
scene_005c.narration: Walking past the pharmacy triggers a memory. Pill bottles rattling, numb warmth spreading through your ribs.

scene_006a.title: Support Line
scene_006a.narration: You talk with a recovery mentor. 'Cravings aren't failure,' they remind you. 'They're part of healing.' Your chest loosens.

scene_006b.title: Quiet Strength
scene_006b.narration: You study with Chloe again. 'You seem better,' she says softly.

scene_006c.title: Tension Rising
scene_006c.narration: You're stretched thin. Your hands shake. Your thoughts blur.

choices.label: Look up your old dealer again

scene_006d.title: Ecstasy
scene_006d.narration: You take a pill. Colored like children's taffy. Warmth blooms immediately, along with guilt. You can hear the giggles of your 14th birthday party, the last time you were truly alive. The world softens, then darkens.

choices.label: Hide it and pretend nothing happened

scene_007a.title: Stability Steps
scene_007a.narration: Your grades stabilize. You breathe easier. You even laugh at a joke.

scene_007b.title: Drifting
scene_007b.narration: You feel suspended. Not falling, not rising. This much silence in your life almost feels threatening.

scene_007c.title: You're Not Alone
scene_007c.narration: Your mentor answers your call. 'Relapse isn't the end,' they say. 'It's information.'

scene_007d.title: Numbness Creeps
scene_007d.narration: You take again. More this time. You convinced yourself that this is all you'll ever be. Your breathing slows. You hear your young cries for your mother to wake up. A friend finds you on the bathroom floor, half conscious and gurgling on your own vomit and calls for help.

scene_008a.title: Spring Hope
scene_008a.narration: The trees are budding. You feel a cautious optimism.

scene_008b.title: Wavering
scene_008b.narration: You feel isolated again. Small triggers surface daily.

scene_008c.title: Wake Up Call
scene_008c.narration: A nurse tells you, 'You're lucky. This could've been worse.' You stare at the ceiling, realizing how close things came. Was this how things were supposed to turn out?

scene_009a.title: Finals Week
scene_009a.narration: You study in the library. It's tough, but you're proud. Your mom calls. It's been a while since you two spoke. She sounds exhausted. You hope that she has kept herself sober. 'You're doing great, baby. Hang in there.'

choices.label: Take a break and speak with her

resource_link.description: Drug addiction doesn't just affect the individual—it sends shockwaves through entire families.

choices.label: Push through, the pressure sinking deeper with her words

scene_009b.title: Close Call
scene_009b.narration: You spot someone from high school. Someone who used like you. You freeze. Jay, was her name. She didn't recover, the syringe wounds never lie.

scene_009c.title: Temptation's Edge
scene_009c.narration: A message pops up on your screen: 'Wanna relax? I got the good stuff that you love.' You hesitate. Your eyes dart between the syringe and eggplant emoji your old 'companion' sent.

scene_010a.title: Going Home
scene_010a.narration: Back in Kensington for the summer. The streets smell like memories and CVS band-aids. Your mom hugs you tightly. 'You're doing better,' she says, voice shaky. You lost weight, but so has she.

choices.label: Stay home and catch up with family

scene_010b.title: Pressure Sinks In
scene_010b.narration: The weight of expectation settles on your shoulders. You keep pushing despite the cost.

scene_011a.title: Family Pressure
scene_011a.narration: You and your mom wash up dishes from dinner, catching up on missed memories and playful banter. A silence washes over the kitchen, and she sighs with a slight smile, 'You're the one who's going to make it out.' It's meant lovingly, but it feels like an added weight. You instantly feel the heat in your eyes well up.

scene_011b.title: Dangerous Familiarity
scene_011b.narration: Morning comes. To get out of the house, you take your old stroll. Under a wire gate, over a hill, into an alleyway between some apartments. You pass the corner where you've used before. A guy nods at you. 'Need anything?'

scene_012.title: Return to Campus
scene_012.narration: You're back at school. You missed the structure. Chloe hugs you. 'I'm glad you're here, Jelly.' You can't help but tear up hearing the nickname she gave you.

choices.label: Join a recovery group again and clubs
Try to manage on your own

scene_013.title: A New Semester
scene_013.narration: You feel different this time. More grounded. Not perfect, but present.

scene_014.title: A Friend in Need
scene_014.narration: A classmate confides that her brother struggles with opioids. You feel the familiar ache of recognition. Especially after hearing he's only 19.

scene_015.title: Trigger Season
scene_015.narration: Cold winds blow. Holidays loom, your old relapse season. You feel the pull knocking at your door.

choices.label: Make a safety plan and text Chloe

scene_016.title: The Test
scene_016.narration: You return home. Your old friend messages: 'You around? I miss you.' Your breath catches.

scene_017a.title: Choosing Yourself
scene_017a.narration: You delete the entire chat. You sit with the ache, but it passes. You made the hard choice.

scene_017b.title: Standing at the Edge
scene_017b.narration: Your friend asks to meet. But you feel a wave of clarity. You don't want this. Not again. Not ever.

scene_018.title: The Turning Point
scene_018.narration: One year. One long, impossible, beautiful year. You sit by a window on New Year's Eve. You whisper to yourself: 'I made it. I'm still here.' Recovery isn't linear. It isn't pretty. But it's yours.
